- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.2) or shows sharp drops, model often fails to anticipate sharp declines; add downward bias or trigger early correction.
- After a price spike (forecast > 85.5), model frequently overcorrects with continued upward trend; cap forecast at 86.5–87.0 for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 85.66 → 80s), model often holds too high; apply exponential decay to forecast toward historical mean over 10–15 days.
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative values (e.g., -0.05, 0.00), model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.0 to forecast for 3–7 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or positive; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5 per day for first 5 days.
- If sentiment is flat or mixed (0.5–0.7), model tends to drift upward; apply smoothing filter or reduce forecast slope by 0.1–0.3 per day.
